title: Basic Brightfield Microscopy

references.label: Biosafety in Microbiological and Biomedical Laboratories (BMBL)

purpose: To correctly set up and use a compound brightfield microscope to observe stained or unstained microbiological specimens at increasing magnification.
principle: Light passes from an illuminator through the specimen and objective lens system, forming a magnified image; brightfield microscopy relies on differences in specimen density/color (often enhanced by staining) for contrast against a bright background.

procedure.instruction: Place the slide on the stage and secure it with the stage clips.
Start with the lowest-power objective (e.g. 4×) and use the coarse focus knob to bring the specimen roughly into focus.
Adjust the condenser and diaphragm for adequate, evenly distributed light.
Center the area of interest, then switch to the next higher objective (e.g. 10×, then 40×), refining focus with the fine focus knob at each step.

For oil immersion (typically 100×), rotate the high-dry objective out of the way, place a drop of immersion oil directly on the slide, then rotate the oil immersion objective into the oil, and fine-focus.
procedure.note: Never let the low- or high-dry objectives touch the oil — oil is used only with the objective specifically designed for it.

procedure.instruction: After use, remove oil from the objective and slide with lens paper per the microscope's cleaning guidance, and return the stage to the lowest-power objective before storing.

observations: Progressive magnification reveals overall field morphology at low power, then increasing structural detail (shape, arrangement, relative size) at higher power.
interpretation: Correct Köhler-style adjustment of light and condenser is what makes fine morphological detail interpretable — poor illumination is a common source of misread morphology, not the specimen itself.
precautions: Always focus by raising, not lowering, the objective when using coarse focus near the slide, to avoid cracking the slide or scratching the objective.
Clean oil off the 100× objective immediately after use.
limitations: Brightfield resolution is limited by the wavelength of visible light (roughly ~0.2 µm at best with oil immersion) and cannot resolve internal structures below that scale; unstained live specimens often have poor contrast under brightfield alone.
biosafetyNotes: Standard aseptic and biosafety precautions apply to handling the specimen on the slide, not to the microscope itself.
